az_yodel_wall.blurb: Yodel Wall is a small cliff within Christopher Creek Gorge in central Arizona, a canyon better known for canyoneering than climbing. Seven routes mix sport, trad and one top rope, with grades running from 5.9 into the 5.11 range, mostly around 5.10. The face points south and is sunny for most of the day, with climbs of roughly 50 to 75 feet. There is no built trail yet, so reaching it means heading toward the neighbouring Memorial Wall first and then working over. Hot summer months are best skipped.

az_boyscout_wall.blurb: Boyscout Wall is a compact sport crag partway up Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains, at about 6,600 feet. Seven bolted lines run from 5.9 to the 5.10 range. The face stands roughly 115 feet, so routes are long for a small cliff and a 70 m rope is wise. It catches sun until late in the day. The stone is unusual for the mountain: gritty near the ground, with smoother holds higher up. A seep or small waterfall can streak the face and may make it unclimbable during monsoon. The approach is a little tricky and finishes with a steep scramble down.

az_courthouse_butte.blurb: Courthouse Butte is a huge mesa just east of Bell Rock, south of Sedona near the Village of Oak Creek. Despite its size there are only a handful of routes, mostly multi-pitch trad, with one aid line. Difficulty spans an easy 5.6 rib up to several 5.11 lines, and the longest climbs run six pitches. It is a serious, adventurous objective rather than a quick crag, and the summit gives wide views. A wide, well-worn trail leads from the Bell Rock trailhead across to the base.

az_lizard_tail_spire.blurb: Lizard Tail Spire is a small spire in the West Sedona and Capitol Butte area, just north of Chimney Rock. Seven short climbs mix trad, bolted and one top-rope line, from an easy 5.1 up through the 5.9 and 5.10 range. Rock quality swings from loose and flaky to solid, so it rewards care. It suits climbers who have finished the nearby Fun Ship routes and want something new. The walk from the Andante trailhead takes around 20 minutes at a slow pace, ending on a use trail heading north.

az_me_and_ewe_crag.blurb: Me and Ewe Crag is a small shaded crag in the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, southeast Arizona. It holds seven routes, mainly trad with a bolted line, and the grades stay moderate, roughly 5.6 through 5.9, which suits newer leaders. Climbers cross a wash and scramble up a gully to reach the base, about 20 minutes from the car. Chain anchors can be spotted on the way in. The wider West Stronghold is a big backcountry dome area, and the dirt road in is rough in places.
